ed1-13.2.1-033: The unchecked rule guarantees the truncated value only when 'the value of the source operand is within the range of the destination type' (PDF p. 131, lines 1-4), so 255.75 -> byte falls to the unspecified-value branch (PDF p. 131, line 5), where the 7th edition guarantees 255 (PDF p. 155, lines 8-10). Every byte result, csc's 255 included, conforms at ISO-1, so no program can observe the difference; the 7th edition rows asserting the truncated value at such edges must not be asserted at ISO-1. ed1-13.2.1-034: 'Otherwise, the result of the conversion is an unspecified value of the destination type' (PDF p. 131, line 5) covers every source outside the range as tested before rounding (PDF p. 131, line 2), including fractional edges such as 255.75 -> byte that the 7th edition maps to 255 (PDF p. 155, lines 8-12). Since any destination value conforms and the conversion succeeds in both editions, no ISO-1 program can observe the difference; NaN and infinities give an unspecified value in both.
